question: Which region grew fastest?
assumptions: region = customer_state
growth = 2017 vs 2018 revenue, Jan-Aug only (both years complete)

notes: Confirmed complete: no LIMIT in query, so this is every state clearing the >=20-orders-in-2017 threshold -- only 10 of Brazil's 27 states/DF qualify, reflecting how concentrated Olist's 2017 order volume was outside SP/major states. Top grower is RN at +186.2%, though its absolute revenue (R$16k -> R$46k) is small -- worth noting the growth leader and the revenue leader (SP) are different states.

notes: Confirmed complete: 20 of 20, matches LIMIT 20. Steepest decline is -98.0%. question: Which category had the highest average order value?
assumptions: replaces the original profit-margin question — Olist has no cost data
'value' = avg price per line item attributed to the category, not full multi-category order totals

notes: Confirmed complete: 10 of 10, matches LIMIT 10. computers leads at R$1,098.92/item but low volume (199 line items) -- a low-volume, high-ticket category. watches_gifts, which dominated Q2's top-revenue-by-product list (6 of the top 20 products), ranks 9th here at R$199.04/item with 5,859 line items -- its revenue comes from volume, not per-unit price. question: Are there unusual sales drops?
assumptions: flags days where revenue < trailing 30-day mean - 2 stddev
first 30 days of the dataset excluded (no trailing window yet)
notes: Confirmed complete: no LIMIT in query, 12 flagged days total. Two distinct clusters: (1) isolated single-day dips in 2017 (Jun 21, Aug 26) -- likely normal noise. (2) 2018-06-30 and 2018-07-07 -- corroborates the May->June 2018 monthly dip from Q1, selected as the Q10 investigation period. (3) 2018-08-22 through 2018-08-29 -- a steadily monotonic decline (20247 -> 1546) over the last 8 days of the dataset. This is almost certainly a dataset-boundary artifact (delivered-status lag near the extraction cutoff), not a genuine demand drop -- consistent with the Aug 2018 caution already noted on Q1. Should NOT be used as a Q10 candidate.

question: Why did revenue decline in a selected period?
expected_value: Revenue fell -12.4% (R$977,545 -> R$856,078) from May to June 2018. This is a genuine demand-side decline, not a data or delivery-status artifact: total orders placed (any status) fell -10.3% in the same window, while the delivered-order completion rate stayed flat (~98%). The decline is best explained by Brazil's nationwide truckers' strike (May 21 - June 1, 2018), which blocked roads across most states, disrupted retail supply chains, and caused Sao Paulo to declare a state of emergency; consumer confidence indicators continued declining into June even as industrial activity began recovering. Supporting evidence: (1) the decline is broad-based across ~10 unrelated categories (watches_gifts, garden_tools, sports_leisure, furniture_decor, cool_stuff, toys, housewares, computers_accessories, office_furniture, small_appliances), consistent with a macro/logistics shock rather than one product or category failing; (2) the decline is geographically concentrated -- Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro alone account for ~85% of the regional revenue drop, matching the strike's epicenter; (3) garden_tools, a bulky freight-dependent category, fell below its own Jan-Mar 2018 baseline in June before recovering in July, consistent with delivery disruption rather than seasonal demand. Two caveats prevent this from being a single clean story: watches_gifts' apparent decline is partly a statistical mirage -- May was inflated by Mother's Day gift buying (mid-May in Brazil), so June's value is actually close to the March-April baseline once the spike is accounted for. And sports_leisure's decline began in March, predating the strike, so it likely has a separate, unidentified cause. Overall verdict: the truckers' strike is the best-supported explanation for the broad, SP/RJ-concentrated, freight-sensitive portion of the June 2018 revenue dip, but it does not explain every contributing category equally.
